A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the risk for hereditary breast carcinoma in women with a personal history for breast carcinoma or ovarian carcinoma is high.
we have shown that there is a high frequency of BRCA1 and/or BRCA2 mutation in patients with breast carcinoma, especially if there is an associated family history.

the prevalence of hereditary breast carcinoma in women with breast or ovarian cancer presenting for mammography is 2.4%, and 1.4% of women in this cohort have a family history suggestive of hereditary ovarian carcinoma syndrome.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prevalence of hereditary breast carcinoma is high in this population, and that it is not limited to women with a strong personal and family history of breast carcinoma.
the risk of breast and ovarian cancer is not the only risk associated with the BRCA1 and 2 genes.
the prevalence of family history in this cohort is high and suggests that the majority of patients with a positive family history are not being referred for genetic counseling.
